what_it_does: Before a chip is manufactured, engineers run static timing analysis (STA) — a process that calculates how long electrical signals take to travel through every path on the chip — to make sure the design will run at its target speed. This analysis must be repeated thousands of times as designers tweak the layout, so speed matters enormously. The problem is that the most accurate STA tools are proprietary commercial products whose internal delay models are secret, making it hard to accelerate them on GPUs without losing accuracy. INSTA solves this by first using the commercial tool to generate a reference dataset once, then training a GPU-accelerated STA engine to mimic that tool's behavior through a fine-tuning step. Because the engine is built with differentiable math (meaning you can compute gradients through it, just like training a neural network), it can also automatically suggest how to resize transistors or move circuit elements to improve timing — going beyond analysis to optimization. The result is timing updates that are reported to be 25 times faster than re-running the commercial tool from scratch.
